title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: build custom engine agents with the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK
summary: Hold for a correction to the upload guidance: Microsoft documents choosing the audience before the permissions-review step, not afterwards. The roadmap facts, catalogue upload path and Graph calls are supported; the governance checklist also names controls missing from the table.

claims.quote: Developers can use the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK to create custom engine agents. These agents, built on their own AI stack

claims.claim: The roadmap says these agents can be deployed to Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Teams and other non-Microsoft channels.
claims.quote: can be deployed to various platforms, including Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Teams, and other non-Microsoft channels.

claims.claim: Custom engine agents require app manifest version 1.21 or later.
claims.quote: Custom engine agents are supported in app manifest version 1.21 and later versions.

claims.claim: Learn documents building and deploying with the SDK in the present tense despite the record's In development status.
claims.quote: The Microsoft 365 Agents SDK enables you to build custom engine agents by using the AI stack of your choice, then deploy them to Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: Custom engine agents give developers control over data integrations and core processing rather than using Copilot's own orchestration.
claims.quote: Unlike standard Copilot experiences, custom engine agents provide full control over orchestration, AI models, and data integrations

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated a default availability for newly published Agents SDK custom engine agents, so defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Agents SDK custom engine agents default availability newly published agents admin enable switch. Read SDK, create-deploy, overview and agent-registry pages; audience selection is documented, but no SDK-agent default is stated.

claims.claim: No source states that introducing the SDK changes existing Copilot behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Agents SDK custom engine agents default availability newly published agents admin enable switch. Read SDK, overview, create-deploy and roadmap record; they describe a development capability, not an automatic change to existing Copilot.

claims.claim: Pro-code Agents SDK agents can use the Retrieval API for grounding in Microsoft 365 data.
claims.quote: and use the Retrieval API for grounding in Microsoft 365 data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center upload flow lets admins review agent permissions before choosing its audience.
claims.quote: 4. Under Publish, select the users or groups who can install the agent. ... 5. Under Deploy (optional), select the users or groups who will have the agent preinstalled. ... 7. Review agent permissions. Then, select Next.
claims.fix: Replace 'before choosing its audience' with 'before finishing deployment' in Risk assessment. Replace 'review the agent permissions step before widening it' with 'review the agent permissions step before finishing deployment' in At rollout; the cited upload flow selects audiences before reviewing permissions.

claims.claim: The cost guidance describes a mixed design with user and administrator licences, usage-based consumption and independently hosted services.

claims.claim: Costs vary by product and distribution route and include development tools as a separate category.
claims.quote: Costs vary by product and distribution route. ... Development tools, test environments, and developer subscriptions.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Custom engine agent builders should budget for orchestration, models and hosting, with Azure AI Foundry, App Service and Azure AI Bot Service pricing given as resources.
claims.quote: budget for your own orchestration, models, and hosting. Existing service pricing resources include Azure AI Foundry pricing, App Service pricing, and Azure AI Bot Service pricing.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot APIs are available at no additional cost to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: The Microsoft 365 Copilot APIs are available at no additional cost to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Support for users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license is currently not available.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A licence or Copilot Credits rate specific to the Agents SDK, including a universal end-user licence for its agents, is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Agents SDK licensing custom engine agents end users Copilot license Copilot Credits pricing; SDK license prerequisites end users. Read cost, FAQ, overview, create-deploy and agent-management licensing; no SDK-specific licence or credit rate found.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Upload new app uploads a custom package to the organisation's catalogue.
claims.quote: Access Teams admin center and go to Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select Upload new app, select Upload, and select the app package that the developer provided to you.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/appCatalogs/teamsApps publishes a Teams app to the tenant catalogue.
claims.quote: Specifically, this API publishes the app to your organization's catalog (the tenant app catalog) ... POST /appCatalogs/teamsApps

claims.claim: Global or Teams administrators can upload custom apps for the organisation in Teams admin center.
claims.quote: Custom app upload by admin | Global or Teams administrators using Teams admin center or using Teams client | Available to entire org; no approval required

claims.claim: The publish API supports delegated permissions only.
claims.quote: Application | Not supported. | Not supported. ... The AppCatalog.Submit permission allows you to submit apps for review only, not to publish them to the catalog.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; controls[1].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Agents > All agents > agent > Block is the documented UI route; its effect examples name Agent Builder, Copilot Studio, SharePoint and Foundry, but not Agents SDK.
claims.quote: Block or unblock agents for the entire organization by using the same controls that work for any other app in the Microsoft 365 admin center. ... Select Agents > All agents. ... select an agent ... select Block or Unblock.
claims.fix: Replace the final sentence of controls[1].note, including the rendered table copy, with 'The UI blocks the selected agent for the organisation; the documented effects across host products vary by agent type.' Remove the Open questions bullet questioning whether this general Block action covers Agents SDK agents.
